- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward historical mean of last 7–10 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from positive to negative), model often fails to adjust; re-estimate with a 1–2% downward bias.
- If model forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
